newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FORGET MANCHESTER UNITED, SAYS SAMMER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FORGET MANCHESTER UNITED, SAYS SAMMER.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund are not allowed to think about next month's mouth-watering European Cup semifinal against Manchester United after suffering their first league defeat at home for more than a year on Saturday.
A few days after clinching their place in the semifinals, the German champions were beaten 3-1 by lowly Borussia Moenchengladbach, their second consecutive Bundesliga defeat.
Dortmund lost their place at the top of the table to VfB Stuttgart.
Although any clash with the English has special significance for German players, Dortmund can only afford to think about domestic matters in the run-up to the European first leg on April 9.
"If we start thinking about Manchester now, then the championship is going to go down the drain," said German international libero Matthias Sammer, who misses the first leg through suspension.

"I hope this does upset things a bit because we can't just accept two defeats in a row. But the important thing now is how the players deal with each other, that they don't lose their mutual respect."

The atmosphere in the Dortmund dressing rooms was somewhat stormy after goals from Swedish striker Martin Dahlin, Pole Andrzej Juskowiak and substitute Jorgen Pettersson exposed huge holes in their defence.

Dortmund, who lost 4-1 at Stuttgart a week ago, last experienced defeat at home in February 1996, going down to Hansa Rostock. The last time the 1995 and 1996 champions lost two league matches in a row was at the end of the 1992-93 season.
"There were one or two disputes (in the dressing rooms) but nothing for public consumption," striker Karlheinz Riedle said.

Sammer added: "After the European Cup, you always have problems finding your rhythm. If you have two games like that you have to analyse them and recognise your mistakes and then things will improve."
Both the Dortmund fans and the club groundsman also need to tighten up their acts before the English champions visit Germany for the first leg.

At the end of the first half the crowd almost lost control after defender Juergen Kohler was sent off. Moenchengladbach midfielder Stefan Effenberg was held up from taking a corner when fans threw plastic cups down at the corner of the pitch.
Sammer had to plead with the bank of Dortmund supporters behind the goal to calm down before the game could continue.
Dortmund have been having problems getting the grass to grow on one side of the pitch because of problems with light following a renovation of the main stand.
The grass in the centre circle also cut up quite badly during the match and players had problems keeping their feet.
